paragraphs: Yitzchak, the father of Rav Nachman.

In [Taanit 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.21b.6), Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak called himself “a maneh, son of a peras.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Taanit.21b.6.1) explains that his father was called simply “Yitzchak” because he had not been ordained. [Haggahot Ya'avetz](https://www.sefaria.org/Haggahot_Ya'avetz_on_Taanit.21b.2), however, explains that the father of Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was not wealthy.[^1]

He had a God-fearing wife, as related in [Shabbat 156b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.156b.6): Chaldean astrologers told her that her son would be a thief. She therefore took care that her son (Rav Nachman) covered his head, and told him: “Cover your head, so that the fear of Heaven will be upon you.”

notes.text: Peras means half a maneh. Rashi explains the contrast in terms of ordination. Ya’avetz takes it as a comparison of wealth, since he sees no reason to read Rav Nachman as disparaging his father.
